Marcus Reed: Dropping perf numbers from the overhead run (w/ cache telemetry v2 hooks behind flag, but enabled). This is from the Drive summary: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/engineering/serving-runtime/cache-instrumentation-overhead-results

Marcus Reed: TL;DR: median looks fine, but we’ve got a couple p95 spikes for long-prefill workloads on A100 when `saved_prefill_ms` is enabled.

Marcus Reed: Paste from the doc (microbench, single-model, batch=auto, seq-len mix as noted). Overhead is (after - before) / before.

```
Scenario                          GPU    Metric        Before     After      Δ
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Short prefill (p50 prompt=256)     L4     p50 latency   31.2 ms    31.4 ms   +0.6%
                                  L4     p95 latency   44.8 ms    45.1 ms   +0.7%
                                  L4     tok/s         19.8k      19.7k     -0.5%

Mixed (prompt=1k, decode=256)      A10G   p50 latency   83.5 ms    84.0 ms   +0.6%
                                  A10G   p95 latency   121.9 ms   123.0 ms  +0.9%
                                  A10G   tok/s         8.2k       8.1k      -0.8%

Long prefill (p50 prompt=4k)       A100   p50 latency   212.4 ms   214.0 ms  +0.8%
                                  A100   p95 latency   289.6 ms   295.9 ms  +2.2%
                                  A100   tok/s         5.1k       5.0k      -1.6%

Cache-heavy (80% hit, prompt=2k)   A100   p50 latency   97.8 ms    98.5 ms   +0.7%
                                  A100   p95 latency   141.3 ms   142.2 ms  +0.6%
                                  A100   tok/s         11.3k      11.2k     -0.9%
```

Marcus Reed: The +2.2% p95 on long-prefill is the only red flag relative to the <1% p95 target in ENG-4813. Everything else is within noise.

Omar El-Sayed: Thanks. That A100 long prefill case is exactly where we do more work per request. Question: is this w/ `cache.telemetry.saved_prefill_ms=true` and `outcome_classification=true` both on?

Marcus Reed: Yep. Both on. I ran 3 variants; the table above is “full v2 payload.” When I turned off `saved_prefill_ms` estimation the p95 delta dropped to ~+1.1%.

Samir Qureshi: That matches my local profiling. The estimator is doing a couple extra atomics + reading some per-layer stats. We can likely move the calculation to the slow path / end-of-request aggregation.

Noah Patel: +1. We shouldn’t compute anything that’s “nice-to-have” on the hot prefill path. We can export raw counters (prefill_tokens, prefill_steps, cache_hit_bytes) and compute saved_prefill_ms downstream.

Logan Wright: Careful: Optimize wants saved_prefill_ms per {route,model,region} quickly. But it doesn’t need it as a per-request exact value. Aggregated estimate is fine.

Thomas Baird: Also check tag handling. If we’re formatting strings for metric labels on each request, that’ll show up worst on the long-prefill (longer request, more instrumentation calls).

Samir Qureshi: We’re not allocating strings per event, but we *are* calling into the telemetry sink for each cache lookup/insert event. For prefill, there can be multiple lookups depending on chunking.

Omar El-Sayed: That’s probably it. We can batch within the request and emit a single struct at end (lookup_count, hit_count, miss_count, hit_bytes_total). We still need enough for classification (hit/miss/partial).

Marcus Reed: FYI the A100 long-prefill trace shows the extra time mostly CPU-side in the request thread, not GPU kernels. Looks like contention in the metrics aggregator lock.

Logan Wright: Ugh. If we’re taking a lock on every lookup, we’ll lose. Can we go lock-free per-thread buffer + flush?

Samir Qureshi: Yep. We already have the request-local `CacheTelemetryContext`. I can change it so the lookup/insert/evict hooks just increment counters in that context (plain ints), then a single export at the end.

Noah Patel: That would also make sampling cleaner. Sample at the request boundary, not event boundary.

Thomas Baird: +1. Sampling should be “decide once per request” and do nothing if not sampled.

Mateo Alvarez: What’s the worst-case overhead if we ship as-is? I don’t want to block the sprint on a microbench edge case, but we also can’t regress p95 by >2% on the long prompt tail.

Marcus Reed: As-is, it’s only showing up in that long-prefill distribution. Real prod might see less, but our acceptance criteria in ENG-4813 is explicit (<1% p95). We should fix.

Omar El-Sayed: Agreed. We’ll take the batching approach. It’s straightforward and reduces contention.

Logan Wright: Works for Telemetry. As long as the exported payload still has: outcome_class (hit/miss/partial), hit_bytes, miss_bytes (or miss_tokens), cacheable_prompt_tokens, and a stable request-level sample flag.

Samir Qureshi: Proposed change list:
1) Lookup/insert/evict hooks -> only increment request-local counters (no sink calls).
2) Emit one event at request end (prefill boundary or completion), containing totals + outcome classification.
3) Defer saved_prefill_ms estimation to aggregator (or compute at end only once).

Noah Patel: Please also sanity check “partial” classification. It’s easy to miscount when we have partial-prefill and streaming retries.

Omar El-Sayed: Yep. I’ll sync with Sofia’s team too—scheduling boundaries might affect where we “end” a request for export.

perf-canary-bot: perf-canary run queued for branch `omar/batch-cache-telemetry` (scenario: cache-heavy, long-prefill). ETA ~35 min.

Marcus Reed: Action items (so we don’t lose track):
- [Samir] Implement request-local batching + single export event (target PR update on top of pr-18421)
- [Omar] Disable per-lookup sink calls; make sampling decision at request start
- [Marcus] Re-run microbench suite after patch; update the Drive table + comment in ENG-4813
- [Thomas] Review sampling + lock contention (anything in sink that still locks)
- [Logan] Confirm downstream pipeline can compute saved_prefill_ms from raw counters (or accept end-of-request computation)

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: I’ll update the spec note: saved_prefill_ms is “estimated; may be computed post-aggregation.”

Mateo Alvarez: Great. Let’s keep the <1% p95 bar. If the patch doesn’t get us there, we can temporarily gate saved_prefill_ms behind an additional flag for long-prefill routes.

Marcus Reed: :+1: Will post updated numbers when the canary completes.

Samir Qureshi: Ack. I’ll push a patch in the next couple hours.

Noah Patel: Please add a quick note in the profiling playbook about “watch for sink lock contention” + how to spot it in pprof.

Marcus Reed: Will do.
